text:
maria: Hey — trying to get the Python SDK installed on my new M1 Mac (macOS 13). `pip install redwood-sdk` falls back to building from source and the build fails with a rust extension error.

maria: Error snippet: ```error: failed to run custom build command for `tokenizers v0.13.2` caused by: could not find OpenSSL library````

maria: pip ends up compiling tokenizers/rust which I want to avoid. Poetry also tries to build when doing `poetry install` and then lockfile ends up including weird platform markers. Anyone seen this?

jamal: yup saw this on an M1 last week. usually pip picks a wheel if there is one for macosx_11_0_arm64 or universal2. if yours is missing, pip will build. which pip version? `pip --version` matters.

maria: pip 23.3.1, python 3.11.2. I upgraded pip just to be sure but same.

kelly: common culprits: (1) upstream didn't publish a macOS arm64 wheel, (2) your CI builds on x86 and wheel tags don't match, or (3) openssl dev headers missing so & tokenizers fails to link. on mac brew `brew install openssl rust` and export `LDFLAGS`/`CPPFLAGS` helps.

sophie: also poetry uses isolated builds (PEP 517) by default, so it will always build from sdist if it thinks a wheel is not compatible. poetry 1.3+ adds editable PEP 660 support which changes behavior for `poetry install` vs `pip install -e .`

maria: I tried brew openssl & rust but still hit the same build error — the log points to a wheel metadata mismatch: `ERROR: Failed to build wheel for redwood-sdk` and then `NOTE: This package only provides source distribution`

jamal: can you paste `pip debug --verbose`? that shows platform tags pip is checking. Also check `python -m pip download redwood-sdk --only-binary=:all:` to see if a binary wheel is available.

maria: ran that, no binary found for macosx_13_arm64; only manylinux wheels were present.

kelly: that's the root cause — we have manylinux wheels for linux but no macos universal2/arm64 wheels published. feature request: prebuilt macOS arm64/universal2 wheels. open an issue?

sophie: agreed. plus we should include a `py.typed` so type checkers don't need to build. and mark `packages`/classifiers correctly so pip identifies compatibility.

maria: opened issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/842 — linked logs + `pip debug`.

devex-bot: CI report: build job #2314 failed on macos-latest during `pip install .` (see logs) :warning:

ci-bot: Re-run suggestion: add a `cibuildwheel` job to produce universal2 wheels and upload to PyPI. many projects use `cibuildwheel --platform macos` or `python -m build` on a mac runner.

jamal: short-term workarounds: (1) use an x86 Python under Rosetta and install an x86 wheel if available, or (2) `pip install --no-build-isolation --no-use-pep517 .` after building wheels locally, or (3) use docker manylinux for linux targets.

maria: for our dev onboarding docs we probably need to add a mac arm troubleshooting section. I wasted 40 min on this.

kelly: agree — also ask release team to publish mac wheels for patch releases. I'll add to release checklist: build universal2 + manylinux2014_x86_64 + manylinux2014_aarch64 via cibuildwheel.

sophie: small SDK packaging bug: typing stubs are in `src/` but we forgot `py.typed` in sdist -> mypy/pyright treat it as untyped when installing from wheel. can we add that to MANIFEST.in?

maria: another nuance: Poetry's lockfile records the platform markers which makes reproducing in CI tricky. `poetry export -f requirements.txt --no-build-isolation` helps as a stopgap.

jamal: I'll draft a PR: add macOS universal2 wheel CI, include `py.typed`, update classifiers, and add a short doc for mac arm installs + fix manifest. linking PR when ready. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — will try the `pip download` check and report back. really appreciate the quick answers!
